title: Final: tasks without await
sub: ContinueWith, schedulers, Parallel, timers and cancellation
cards/0/q: A WPF button handler, not inside any task. Where does Heavy() run?
cards/0/options/0: On the pool: outside a task TaskScheduler.Current is Default
cards/0/options/1: On the UI thread: StartNew takes the current SynchronizationContext
cards/0/options/2: On the UI thread: StartNew without a scheduler takes Current
cards/0/options/3: On a new dedicated thread: that is how StartNew works by default
cards/0/explain: Current is the scheduler of the running task, not the thread's context. A button handler is not a task, so Current is Default. The trap fires only when the code is already inside a task on a UI scheduler. It is safer not to guess and to write Task.Run.
cards/1/q: Which line throws TaskCanceledException whatever the outcome of LoadAsync?
cards/1/explain: Of the two continuations one is always skipped and moves to Canceled: on success it is log, on failure it is show. WhenAll with a cancelled task is cancelled too, and await throws TaskCanceledException.
cards/2/q: How does Task.Run(work) differ from Task.Factory.StartNew(work)? Select all.
cards/2/options/2: Task.Run unwraps the Task<Task> from an async lambda
cards/2/options/3: Task.Run allocates a dedicated thread for long work
cards/2/options/4: Task.Run picks up the caller's cancellation token by itself
cards/2/explain: Task.Run = StartNew with DenyChildAttach, TaskScheduler.Default and Unwrap for async lambdas. Only LongRunning gives a dedicated thread, and Task.Run uses only a token passed to it explicitly.
cards/3/q: Inside Task.Run a library creates a task with AttachedToParent and throws from it. What does await on your task see?
cards/3/options/0: Nothing: the child did not attach, its error stays in its own task
cards/3/options/1: An AggregateException with the child's error
cards/3/options/2: Your task waits for the child and completes together with it
cards/3/explain: DenyChildAttach on the Task.Run task silently turns the child into an independent task. No waiting, no foreign exceptions. The child's error is the concern of whoever created it.
cards/4/q: You need a report in the source row order, but the heavy formula should run on all cores. What do you add?
cards/4/explain: AsOrdered makes PLINQ return results in the source order while computing them in parallel. WithDegreeOfParallelism(1) kills the parallelism, and OrderBy sorts by value, not by position.
cards/5/q: A PeriodicTimer has a 5 s period, and the work in the loop takes 8 s. How do the runs go?
cards/5/options/0: Back to back: one missed tick is pending, extra ones do not pile up
cards/5/options/1: Overlapping: a new instance starts every 5 s
cards/5/options/2: Every 10 s: a missed tick postpones the next one
cards/5/options/3: Missed ticks accumulate, and the loop catches up on them
cards/5/explain: While the work runs, the timer remembers at most one tick. The next wait completes immediately, and the work takes 8 s again. No overlap: a new iteration does not start until you return to WaitForNextTickAsync.
cards/6/q: A background thread (IsBackground = true) is writing a file in try/finally when Main ends. What about finally?
cards/6/options/0: It does not run: the runtime stops background threads without an exception
cards/6/options/2: It runs: on exit a ThreadAbortException is raised in the thread
cards/6/options/3: The process waits until the background thread finishes the file
cards/6/explain: Background threads do not hold the process. When the last foreground thread ends, they are cut off where they are, and finally does not run. For a clean exit — a cancellation token and waiting for the work.
cards/7/q: Cancel the request if the caller cancels or 10 seconds pass, and leave no subscription on someone else's token
cards/7/explain: The linked source is cancelled for either reason, CancelAfter adds the timeout, and using removes the subscription on ct when the method ends.
cards/8/q: Match them and test yourself on the whole unit
cards/8/pairs/0/1: A task that waits for the inner task
cards/8/pairs/1/1: A dedicated thread for blocking work
cards/8/pairs/2/1: Finish the iterations with lower indices
cards/8/pairs/3/1: A continuation without the scheduler queue
